text: A torque meter is calibrated to reference standards of mass, length and time each with $5%$ accuracy. After calibration, the measured torque with this torque meter will have net accuracy of :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know that, torque applied on a rotating body,

$\begin{array}{ll} τ & =\text{Force}\times \text{Perpendicular distance} \\  \\ \Rightarrow \quad [τ] & =\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ][\mathrm{L}]\Rightarrow [τ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ] \end{array}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{\Delta τ}{τ}=\frac{\Delta M}{M}+2\frac{\Delta L}{L}+2\frac{\Delta T}{T}$

$=5\times 5%=25%$

text: A bag is gently dropped on a conveyor belt moving at a speed of $2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The coefficient of friction between the conveyor belt and bag is $0.4$. Initially, the bag slips on the belt before it stops due to friction. The distance travelled by the bag on the belt during slipping motion, is : [Take $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Speed of conveyor belt, $v=2\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

Coefficient of friction between the conveyor belt and bag, $μ=0.4$

Acceleration of bag due to slipping motion,

$a=μg=0.4\times 10=4\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\left (\because g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$

If $s$ be the distance travelled by the bag on the belt during slipping motion, then

$v^{2}=u^{2}-2as$

$\Rightarrow 0=v^{2}-2as$

$\Rightarrow s=\frac{v^{2}}{2a}=\frac{2^{2}}{2\times 4}=0.5\mathrm{m}$

text: Two sources of equal emfs are connected in series. This combination is connected to an external resistance R. The internal resistances of the two sources are $r_{1}$ and $r_{2}$ $(r_{1}>r_{2})$. If the potential difference across the source of internal resistance $r_{1}$ is zero, then the value of R will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The two sources of emf $ε$ are in series, aiding each other, with the external resistance $R$, so the current is

$I=\dfrac{2ε}{r_{1}+r_{2}+R}$

The potential difference across the terminals of the source with internal resistance $r_{1}$ is $V_{1}=ε-Ir_{1}$. For $V_{1}=0$:

$Ir_{1}=ε\Rightarrow \dfrac{2ε\quad r_{1}}{r_{1}+r_{2}+R}=ε$

$2r_{1}=r_{1}+r_{2}+R\Rightarrow R=r_{1}-r_{2}$

Since $r_{1}>r_{2}$, this $R$ is positive; $r_{2}-r_{1}$ is negative and cannot be a resistance here.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: A microscope was initially placed in air (refractive index 1). It is then immersed in oil (refractive index 2). For a light whose wavelength in air is $λ$, calculate the change of microscope's resolving power due to oil and choose the correct option.
options: Resolving power will be $\frac{1}{4}$ in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be twice in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be four times in the oil than it was in the air.
Resolving power will be $\frac{1}{2}$ in the oil than it was in the air.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The resolving power of a microscope is determined by the Rayleigh criterion, which states that it is inversely proportional to the wavelength of light used in the medium in which the microscopy is being performed. Mathematically, the resolving power (RP) can be represented as:

$RP=\frac{1}{λ_{n}}$

where $λ_{n}$ is the wavelength of light in the medium, which can be found using the formula:

$λ_{n}=\frac{λ}{n}$

Here, $λ$ is the wavelength of light in vacuum (or air, for practical purposes, since their refractive indices are close enough), and $n$ is the refractive index of the medium.

In air, the refractive index $n=1$, so the wavelength of light in air ($λ_{air}$) is equal to $λ$.

In oil, the refractive index $n=2$, so the wavelength of light in oil ($λ_{oil}$) is $λ/2$.

Therefore, the change in resolving power when moving from air to oil can be calculated as the ratio of resolving powers in oil to air:

$\frac{RP_{oil}}{RP_{air}}=\frac{λ_{air}}{λ_{oil}}=\frac{λ}{λ/2}=2$

This means that the resolving power in oil is twice that in air. Thus, the correct option is:

Option B: Resolving power will be twice in the oil than it was in the air.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: An electron (mass $\mathrm{m}$) with an initial velocity $⃗{v}=v_{0}\hat{i}(v_{0}>0)$ is moving in an electric field $⃗{E}=-E_{0}\hat{i}(E_{0}>0)$ where $E_{0}$ is constant. If at $\mathrm{t}=0$ de Broglie wavelength is $λ_{0}=\frac{h}{mv_{0}}$, then its de Broglie wavelength after time t is given by
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\text{At}t=0,λ_{0}=\frac{h}{mv_{0}}$

Since $⃗{v}=v_{0}\hat{i}$ and $\vec{\mathrm{E}}=-\mathrm{E}_{0}\hat{i}$

its velocity $v$ at any time $t$ is given by

$v=v_{o}+\frac{e\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{o}}}{m}t$

De Broglie wavelength $λ$ at any time $t$ is given by

$\begin{array}{ll} λ & =\dfrac{h}{mv}=\dfrac{h}{m\left (v_{0}+\frac{e\mathrm{E}_{0}}{m}t\right )} \\  \\ =\dfrac{h}{mv_{0}\left (1+\frac{e\mathrm{E}_{0}}{mv_{0}}t\right )} \\  \\ =\dfrac{λ_{0}}{1+\frac{e\mathrm{E}_{0}}{mv_{0}}t} \end{array}$

text: To light, a $50\mathrm{W},100\mathrm{V}$ lamp is connected, in series with a capacitor of capacitance $\frac{50}{π\sqrt{x}}μF$, with $200\mathrm{V},50\mathrm{Hz}\mathrm{AC}$ source. The value of $x$ will be $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The lamp is rated $50\text{W}$, $100\text{V}$, so

$R=\frac{V^{2}}{P}=\frac{100^{2}}{50}=200\Omega ,I=\frac{P}{V}=\frac{50}{100}=0.5\text{A}$

For the lamp to glow normally, $100\text{V}$ must appear across it. In the series $RC$ circuit $V_{R}$ and $V_{C}$ are $90^{\circ }$ apart, so

$V_{C}=\sqrt{200^{2}-100^{2}}=100\sqrt{3}\text{V}\Rightarrow X_{C}=\frac{V_{C}}{I}=\frac{100\sqrt{3}}{0.5}=200\sqrt{3}\Omega$

With $C=\dfrac{50}{π\sqrt{x}}\times 10^{-6}\text{F}$ and $f=50\text{Hz}$,

$X_{C}=\frac{1}{2πfC}=\frac{π\sqrt{x}}{2π\times 50\times 50\times 10^{-6}}=\frac{\sqrt{x}\times 10^{6}}{5000}=200\sqrt{x}\Omega$

So $200\sqrt{x}=200\sqrt{3}$, which gives $x=3$.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: A mass $0.9\mathrm{kg}$, attached to a horizontal spring, executes SHM with an amplitude $\mathrm{A}_{1}$. When this mass passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass of $124\mathrm{g}$ is placed over it and both masses move together with amplitude $A_{2}$. If the ratio $\frac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}$ is $\frac{α}{α-1}$, then the value of $α$ will be $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At the mean position the spring exerts no force, so horizontal momentum is conserved when the $124\text{g}$ mass is placed on the moving block, and the mean position stays the same:

$m_{1}v_{1}=(m_{1}+m_{2})v_{2},m_{1}=0.9\text{kg},m_{1}+m_{2}=1.024\text{kg}$

At the mean position the speed is maximum, $v=Aω$ with $ω=\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$:

$0.9A_{1}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{0.9}}=1.024A_{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{1.024}}\Rightarrow A_{1}\sqrt{0.9}=A_{2}\sqrt{1.024}$

$\dfrac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1.024}{0.9}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{1024}{900}}=\dfrac{32}{30}=\dfrac{16}{15}$

Comparing with $\dfrac{α}{α-1}$ gives $α=16$.

Hence, the answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 27th July Morning Shift

text: A pulley of radius $1.5\mathrm{m}$ is rotated about its axis by a force $F=\left (12\mathrm{t}-3\mathrm{t}^{2}\right )N$ applied tangentially (while t is measured in seconds). solution.body:

$FR=Iα$

$α=\frac{(12t-3t^{2})\times 1.5}{4.5}=4t-t^{2}$

$w=\int αdt=2t^{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}$

$w=0$

$\Rightarrow t^{2}\left [2-\frac{t}{3}\right ]=0$

$θ=\int\limits _{0}^{6}\left [2t^{2}-\frac{t^{3}}{3}\right ]dt=\left [\frac{2t^{3}}{3}-\frac{t^{4}}{12}\right ]\left |_{0}^{6} \right.$

$=\left [\frac{2}{3}\times 6^{3}-\frac{6^{4}}{12}\right ]=36$

$n=\frac{36}{2π}$

$=\frac{18}{π}$
